anchor.desc: feet on native row 168 (same as warden.png); body centred at x=78. Every layer sheet uses exactly the body grid, so all layers are drawn at the same (x, y) as the body sprite.

views.front: enemy side: 3/4 front, facing screen-left (like P1 troops)
views.back: player side: seen from behind (like warden.png row 2); attacks go toward the top-right

animationNotes.rows: shared rows (idle, hit, death, rout) are drawn for every weapon: the weapon layer of the equipped kind has those rows too. Weapon rows (windup_/attack_/recover_<kind>) only have content in that kind's weapon sheets.
animationNotes.idle: loops. Weapon carried at rest. The lantern is in the off hand, except with the "-belt" lantern variants (use them with bow, crossbow and shields), which hang it on the belt in every row.
animationNotes.hit: frame 0 is a built-in brightness flash that stays inside the ramps (palette-swap safe).
animationNotes.death: weapon and a hand-held lantern are dropped from frame 2 (they lie on the ground in the weapon and lantern layers). A belt lantern and a shield stay on the body.
animationNotes.rout: frame 0 = turning in the same view; frames 1-3 = running away, drawn from the other side (front sheet: seen from behind; back sheet: running toward the camera). Play once, then loop frames 1-3.
animationNotes.attack: sword = forehand slash; spear = thrust (front: low toward bottom-left, back: toward top-right); bow = nock, half draw, full draw -> loose (spawn arrow on attack frame 0); crossbow = raise, aim -> shot with recoil (spawn bolt on attack frame 0); axe = overhead chop; mace = overhead smash. No smear trails are baked in: use combat-vfx.png effects on the attack frames.

layers.parts: a part is one depth slice of an item: "<view>:<draw site>" (e.g. front:w_front = weapon held in front of the body, back:a_larm = near arm armour). "@front"/"@back" parts belong to rout frames 1-3, which are drawn in the other rig. A sheet only has the parts it uses; missing parts are simply skipped.
compositeRule: 1. outlines: warden-<view>-body-outline.png, then the "outline" sheet of every worn item in outlineOrder (= the order of each slot's first entry in "order")

2. content: walk "order"; "body" = warden-<view>-body.png; "<slot>.<part>" = items[slot][variant].sheets[view][part] if that item is worn and has the part (parts of the other view never exist, so one list serves both views)
3. head-slot hood colours (items.hood): when one is worn, draw its part instead of the cloak part with the same key
Every pixel is fully opaque or fully transparent, so plain alpha-over is exact (this is what heroArt.js sheetsFor already does).
layers.exactness: rev 2: layer-safe shading. A pixel's colour only depends on the body, the shared cloak silhouette and its own layer (no cross-layer cast shadows or edge shading), and each outline pixel belongs to one layer. A composited loadout is therefore identical to a direct render of the same loadout; see verification.
layers.contexts: body = body + standard cloak context (the cloak is always worn: pick one of the 3 variants). Each other item was cut from a render of body + green cloak + that item alone, so it holds exactly the pixels it owns in that frame (depth is already baked per frame). The 3 cloak variants share the standard silhouette; fur and oilskin only add outside it (collar, rain cape, fringe), so every item fits every cloak.
layers.phaser: load each sheet as a spritesheet (frameWidth 156, frameHeight 174). For a unit, add one Sprite per worn part at the same position, all in one Container (outlines first, then content in order), and play the same animation key on each. Or bake per loadout to a RenderTexture at load time.

standard.note: carried in the off hand (sword / spear / axe / mace rows), on the belt in bow and crossbow rows

hooded.note: carried in the off hand (sword / spear / axe / mace rows), on the belt in bow and crossbow rows

standard-belt.note: the same lantern hung on the belt in EVERY row (idle, hit, death, rout and all attack rows). Use it with bow, crossbow and any shield, so the lantern never jumps.

hooded-belt.note: the same lantern hung on the belt in EVERY row (idle, hit, death, rout and all attack rows). Use it with bow, crossbow and any shield, so the lantern never jumps.

patched.replaces: the cloak part with the same key (front:hood, back:hood, front:hood@back, back:hood@front)

mossweave.replaces: the cloak part with the same key (front:hood, back:hood, front:hood@back, back:hood@front)

nightglass.replaces: the cloak part with the same key (front:hood, back:hood, front:hood@back, back:hood@front)

buckler-good.name: Oak Buckler
buckler-good.desc: oak, steel rim + domed steel boss

buckler-fine.name: Oak Buckler
buckler-fine.desc: oak, brass rim, brass boss and 6 brass studs

kite-basic.name: League Kite Shield
kite-basic.desc: painted face (chipped to the wood), iron rim, iron boss

kite-good.name: League Kite Shield
kite-good.desc: painted face with a pale, steel rim + boss

kite-fine.name: League Kite Shield
kite-fine.desc: painted face with a chevron, brass rim, brass boss and rivets

qualities.basic: dull iron (iron ramp: no white glint), plain wood grip, no fittings
qualities.good: steel (metal ramp, bright glint) with fullers / langets / leather-wrapped grip
qualities.fine: steel with brass guard, pommel, ferrule or bands, recurve bow tips, brass crossbow inlay

anchors.desc: weaponHand = centre of the weapon fist, offHand = lantern/second hand (the rear crossbow hand; also the shield grip), shieldCentre = centre of the buckler / kite face (rows that show a shield), weaponTip = blade tip / spear point / axe or mace head / bow top or nocked arrow tip / crossbow nose. Shared rows list a tip per kind. projectileSpawn on attack frame 0: bow = the bow grip (the arrow has just left), crossbow = the nose.

palette.swapHint: cloak = the Warden hood + cloak and the faction colour (swap this ramp for a faction). furcloak / oilskin are the other cloak variants (swap them the same way if a faction version is needed). tunic, hose, jerkin = clothing; iron (basic) / metal (good, fine) / brass (fine fittings) / wood / fletch = weapons; gambeson / metal = armour; glow = lantern light. Every material is its own ramp dark->light, so a recolour is a straight colour-for-colour swap. Checked in code: no colour outside these ramps + 2 outline colours; alpha only 0/255.

nesMapping.paletteSource: reference/nes-palette.js (exact colours only; alpha 0 or 255; no anti-aliasing)

skin.why: as P1: face T, shade a, R only for the deepest crease.

hair.why: as P1: one flat D mass under the hood.

leather.why: as P1: boots, belt, straps D; O only as a highlight.

wood.why: as P1: shafts and hafts O with a K underside, C glint.

metal.why: as P1: steel S/s with a w glint. On the walker only "good"/"fine" steel gets the w glint (see iron).

cloak.why: Warden green hood + cloak = G body with n for the inner shadow of the hood. Rev 2 (Ronja: the Warden stays green): the Warden owns G and n, and the g highlight was dropped so the Warden never uses a Covenant key. The Covenant moves to t/g/l (see covenant-green-proposal.json).

tunic.why: olive tunic/arm wraps. NES has no desaturated olive, and G would merge with the cloak, so it is grey S like the P1 cloth2 hose. The 16-bit colour stays olive (dE is high, noted).

hose.why: dark hose K with S where lit. Legs read as dark, and the D boots split them from the K outline.

jerkin.why: brown leather jerkin D, lifted to O on the lit edge. It is one step apart from hair D, but the hood face-opening separates them.

glow.why: lantern light apricot a, with a C/w core and an E rim. Y/y (the Lab-nearest) are League gold and are kept free.

iron.why: basic weapons: grey S with a K shade and never a w glint. Good/fine steel (metal ramp) gets the w glint, so quality still reads at 8-bit.

brass.why: fine fittings = O with a C glint (like P2 gilt). y is avoided (League).

gambeson.why: padded armour: tan O with C quilting lines, same language as the P1 tan jack. The 16-bit ramp was warmed from grey khaki so both tiers agree.

furcloak.why: warm fur cloak: D body, O tips, C frost glint. The 16-bit ramp was warmed from grey-brown to fox brown so it reads warm and maps to D/O.

oilskin.why: oilskin: slate S body with K folds and an s sheen streak. The 16-bit ramp was shifted from olive-brown to slate so it maps to S and cannot merge with the D jerkin.

paint.why: as P1: kite shield face E, shade R, glint a (same ramp as the troop shields).

patchwool.why: patched hood: worn brown wool, O body with D shade (lighter than the D hair so the face opening still reads). Patches use the tunic (S) and gambeson (O/C) mappings.

mossweave.why: Mossweave Cowl (Covenant piece) = the proposed Covenant jade: t shade, g body, l light. Never G/n (Warden).

nightglass.why: Nightglass Hood (Nightglass piece) = indigo p body, violet P light, K shade (the Nightglass keys).

fleece.why: sheepskin and hare fur: cream C with an O shade, D/K underside.

outline.why: as P1: both outline rings become black K.

nesMapping.avoid: Y/y (League) are never used. Warden colours own G/n; g/l/t only appear on the Covenant Mossweave Cowl and P/p only on the Nightglass Hood (faction pieces). See covenant-green-proposal.json.
nesMapping.dENote: dE = Lab distance (p1_nes.de) from the 16-bit colour to the chosen NES colour.

walkers8bit.canvas: 16x22 per frame, 4 frames in a 64x22 strip (A contact, B passing, C contact, D passing), facing right, feet on row 21, body centre x=8

layers.grid: every layer strip is 64x22 on the same grid as the full strips (no offsets); alpha 0/255; draw in "order" with plain alpha-over
layers.outlineRule: each layer carries its own K outline, except where it touches the body+cloak silhouette (the body/cloak outline already covers that)
layers.body: legs, face, hair, jerkin, tunic and the K outline that touches them (holes where the cloak goes: always draw a cloak layer; there is no "no cloak" walker)
layers.cloak: hood + cloak placeholders mapped per variant (green G/n, fur O/D/C, oilskin S/K/s) + the variant extras
layers.hood: head-slot hood colours: recolour only the hood pixels (rows 0-8 of the body art) and are drawn over the cloak
layers.armour: recolours the jerkin (padded O/C, mail s/S checker + mail skirt, plate s/S/w + steel skirt); the belt stays on top
layers.lantern: "<v>" = rear hand (sword/spear/axe/mace); "<v>-belt" = hung at the rear hip. Use -belt with bow, crossbow and any shield (same rule as the 16-bit sheets)
layers.shield: on the rear arm, x 0-4 (buckler O/D wood, kite R/E paint like the P1 shields); fist T at x 4
layers.trinket: harefoot: O cap + C fur at x 11, rows 15-17 (front of the belt)
layers.check: walkers_export.py rebuilt 5400 combinations (3 cloaks x 5 helmets x 6 weapons x 3 qualities x shields/none x armour x hood) from the saved layer PNGs and compared them with the direct strips: 0 mismatches

walkers8bit.source: src/warden/walkers8.py (ASCII layers in NES keys; placeholders H/h/j = cloak body/shadow/highlight)

atlas.note: every cloak x helmet (incl. sheepskin) x weapon at quality "good"; bow and crossbow rows carry the belt lantern (rev 2)

qualities.cue: basic = S steel with no w glint (iron); good = s steel with a w glint; fine = glint + O brass fittings. Bow: basic D stave, good/fine O stave, fine C nocks. Buckler: basic S boss, good s/w steel, fine C studs. Kite: basic E stripe, good s steel rib, fine O brass cross + C boss. The weapon difference is only 1-2 px, so on the road it is a hint, not a readable tier.

walkers8bit.checked: every pixel of every saved strip and layer is a key of reference/nes-palette.js (exact RGB), alpha 0/255; Y/y never used. The Warden itself uses G/n only (no g); g/l/t appear only on the Mossweave Cowl hood layer and p/P only on the Nightglass Hood layer.

readability.weaponType: sword, spear, axe, mace, bow and crossbow each have their own silhouette in the front hand (x 12-15)
readability.cloak: green G/n, fur O/D/C with a C collar and ragged hem, oilskin S/K/s with a sheen streak and a rain-cape line
readability.helmet: none shows the green hood; cap = grey dome; kettle = dome + wide brim; nasal = pointed cone + nose bar; sheepskin = cream C roll + D crown

shield.note: the shield is on the off arm in every row of the shared rows and the sword/axe/mace/spear rows; the shield sheets have no content in the bow/crossbow rows. Shield and lantern share the game's Off hand slot; if a loadout has both (e.g. a crew role), use the lantern's "-belt" variant.

lantern.rule: use "<v>-belt" whenever the weapon is a bow or crossbow, or a shield is worn. Then the lantern hangs on the belt in idle, hit, death, rout and every attack row, so it never jumps from hand to hip. With sword/spear/axe/mace and no shield use the hand variant.

hood.rule: head-slot hood colours: draw items.hood[v] parts instead of the cloak parts with the same key; work with every cloak variant and every helmet (helmets sit over the hood).

game.sheepskin_hat: helmet sheepskin (+ hood patched for the brown look, optional)

trinket.rule: belt charm (Hare's-foot Charm): optional, works with everything

verification.palette: every opaque pixel of every sheet is a colour of palette.ramps or one of the 2 outline colours; alpha only 0/255 (export.py asserts).
verification.frameBounds: no layer touches a frame edge in any frame (export.py asserts), including the lengthened spear and both shields.
verification.compositeVsDirect: verify.py composites 11 loadouts (all 6 weapons, all 3 cloaks, all armours, both shields in 2-3 qualities, all 3 hood colours, sheepskin hat, belt charm, belt lanterns) only from the exported PNGs + this JSON, exactly as layers.compositeRule (= heroArt.js sheetsFor) says, and compares them with a direct render in every frame: 0 of 6,021,020 opaque px differ (0.0000%), silhouettes identical. Rev 1 was 3-6% off.
verification.walkers: walkers_export.py rebuilt 5400 combinations (3 cloaks x 5 helmets x 6 weapons x 3 qualities x shields/none x armour x hood) from the saved layer PNGs and compared them with the direct strips: 0 mismatches

what: shields: Oak Buckler and League Kite Shield in basic / good / fine, front (face) and back (inside, straps) on every frame; compatible with sword, axe, mace, spear (see compatibility.shield); per-frame shieldCentre anchors

lantern: new "-belt" variants hang the lantern on the belt in EVERY row (idle, hit, death, rout, all attacks). Rule: use them with bow, crossbow and shields (compatibility.lantern). A belt lantern is not dropped in the death row.

compositing: layer-safe shading (no cross-layer shading; outline pixels owned by one layer) -> composite == direct render, 0.0000% (was 3-6%). Outline sheets are pushed in the order of each slot's first entry in layers.order (as heroArt.js does).

layers: parts are now fine depth slices "<view>:<site>" (e.g. front:w_front) instead of under/over/top; layers.order is one list for both views. 352 sheets (was 180). heroArt.js sheetsFor works unchanged with the new order.

spear: lengthened to the P1 spear (shaft 60.4 + head 15.8 = 76 native units, same as P1 spearmen); the front attack/windup hands moved 2-2.5 units toward the body and windup angles eased so the tip stays inside the 156 px frame. Frame not widened.
back view: mail shows below the cape (hauberk skirt to just above the knee + full mail sleeves); plate adds culet lames, rerebraces on the upper arms, the mail skirt, pauldrons and greaves.

walkers: separable layers on the same 16x22 grid (body, armour, cloak, hood, helmet, trinket, lantern, shield, weapon), quality strip extended to all 6 weapons + both shields (24 rows); atlas adds the sheepskin hat (90 rows).
extras: hood colours (patched, mossweave, nightglass), sheepskin hat, belt charm (harefoot).
Covenant: covenant-green-proposal.json + hubert-previews/warden-vs-covenant-green.png; the Warden walker/NES cloak drops g (Warden = n/G only).
helmet/hood class: the hood is its own shading class so hood colours are exact with every cloak variant; the hood's inner shadow ring also darkens the cloak around the face opening (as before).

weakSpots: no "no cloak" body: the body sheet holds the green cloak and every item was cut with the cloak present, so a bare Warden needs a second set of body/armour/weapon sheets (not done).

the lantern rule needs one line in the game: heroArt.js loadoutOf should append "-belt" to the lantern for bow/crossbow (and if a shield + lantern ever meet). Without it the hand lantern still moves to the belt in the bow/crossbow rows.

shield vs lantern: the game puts both in the Off hand slot, so in practice it is one or the other; HERO_GEAR_MAP.off needs oak_buckler -> shield buckler-good and league_kite_shield -> shield kite-fine (lantern none).
the League Kite Shield is in the neutral P1 paint (red-orange); a League gold version is a straight swap of the paint ramp.
the front-view buckler is small (it reads at 1x, but it is a hint at 8-bit: 5x5 px).
layer-safe shading removes item-on-body cast shadows (e.g. a raised weapon no longer darkens the hood). It is subtle, but the figures are a touch flatter where items overlap.
hood colour layers recolour the cloak's hood only; the mantle/cape stays the cloak colour (as the game splits Head and Cloak).
many sheets (352, 7.5 MB): the game loads ~20-40 PNGs per loadout; bake per loadout (as heroArt.js does) rather than stacking sprites.
Covenant green is a proposal only; registry.js / sprites8.js still use the old sage (G/g) Covenant until someone applies it.
the figure is a 3/4 view (like P1 troops) and a little chunkier and more contrasted than the softer, frontal warden.png.
